findings.issue_text: [BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with only `pass`, leaving the abstract methods get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data unimplemented, so instantiation raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class. Any code path that instantiates this handler (e.g. Detector.detector_handler constructing handler_class(self) for a detector whose type resolves to this grouptype) crashes with TypeError instead of returning the previous no-op handler; even if instantiation were forced, StatefulDetectorHandler's evaluate/commit paths would hit the missing `counter_names` attribute with AttributeError. Previously the class was concrete with a stub `evaluate` returning [].

[BUG] TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence with group_key "val1" while the evaluated group key is "group_key" (the expected DetectorEvaluationResult.group_key is "group_key"), so the occurrence fingerprints differ and the equality assertion fails. The test errors on every CI run: handler.evaluate_group_key_value("group_key", ...) calls build_occurrence_and_event_data with "group_key", producing fingerprint(handler.build_fingerprint("group_key")), but the expected occurrence uses build_fingerprint("val1"); since DetectorEvaluationResult compares result (an IssueOccurrence dataclass including fingerprint) field-wise, the assert never matches and the suite is red.

[ADVISORY] The `value` parameter of build_mock_occurrence_and_event is never referenced in the function body, so the test helper's occurrence is identical regardless of the value, and test_state_results_multi_group builds occurrence_2 with value 6 even though the packet carries group_2: 10. Anyone relying on these tests to verify that the evaluated value is threaded through the new build_occurrence_and_event_data hook gets no verification — a regression that drops or corrupts `value` (e.g. a future real handler embedding the value in evidence_data or the title) would pass this suite; the dead parameter also invites the exact value/6-vs-10 mismatch already present in test_state_results_multi_group.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler is switched to subclass StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing the newly-added abstract method build_occurrence_and_event_data, so any instantiation of it raises TypeError. StatefulDetectorHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data is declared @abc.abstractmethod (src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py, new lines ~166-171); `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass` implements only the inherited evaluate, so Python's ABC machinery makes the class abstract and `group_type.detector_handler(self)` (Detector.detector_handler) raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` the moment any metric-alert detector of this type is processed. The old body (`evaluate` returning `[]`) was instantiable; this one is not. Today it is example code so no user is hit yet, but the first real detector registered with this handler type crashes at dispatch time.

[ADVISORY] The duplicate-group-key guard (logger.error "Duplicate detector state group keys found" plus skip) is deleted and replaced by dict assignment, so duplicate group keys now silently collapse last-wins with no error signal, and the only test covering that path (test_state_results_multi_group_dupe) was removed with no replacement. When a handler returns two results with the same group_key, `results[result.group_key] = result` silently overwrites the first result, so one occurrence is dropped without any log/metric. The old code explicitly logged this as an investigate-now anomaly; that telemetry and its regression test disappear together, so a handler bug producing duplicate keys will go undetected instead of paging anyone.

[ADVISORY] In test_state_results_multi_group the expected occurrence for group_2 is built with value 6 while the packet sets group_2 to 10, and build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores its `value` argument entirely, so the test cannot detect the production code passing the wrong metric value into occurrence building. The literal 6 for group_2 (packet is {"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10}) is a typo that is invisible to the assertion because build_mock_occurrence_and_event never reads `value`. If evaluate_group_key_value ever passed the wrong value (e.g., the dedupe value or a stale counter) to build_occurrence_and_event_data, every test in this file would still pass — the value-propagation contract of the new hook has zero verification.

[ADVISORY] The resolve path (new_status == OK) newly produces a StatusChangeMessage that now reaches create_issue_occurrence_to_kafka via process_detectors, but no test in this diff exercises process_detectors end-to-end with a deactivating group value to verify the STATUS_CHANGE payload. Scanning the diff for test-shaped files, the only test file touched is tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py; its process_detectors tests (test, test_state_results, test_state_results_multi_group) all assert only the OCCURRENCE trigger path, while test_above_below_threshold stops at handler.evaluate and never runs the producer. The StatusChangeMessage branch is newly reachable in this diff (the old code set `result = None` with a TODO), so a regression in how create_issue_occurrence_from_result serializes status changes (e.g., wrong payload_type or dropping event_data=None) would ship unnoticed.

[ADVISORY] The public signatures of process_detectors and DetectorHandler.evaluate change their result shape from list[DetectorEvaluationResult] to dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult] without any consumer outside the abstract base being updated in this diff. Any caller of process_detectors or any concrete DetectorHandler subclass outside this diff (out-of-tree handlers, sibling processors that consume the (detector, results) tuples) that iterates the second element expecting DetectorEvaluationResult objects will instead iterate group keys and fail with AttributeError on `.result`/`.group_key`, silently or at runtime depending on typing enforcement. The diff updates only the base class and this file's own tests.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler is converted to a StatefulDetectorHandler subclass with `pass` while StatefulDetectorHandler declares three abstract methods (get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), leaving the class uninstantiable. The old stub was a concrete DetectorHandler whose evaluate() returned [] safely; the replacement raises TypeError at construction. Any Detector whose type slug resolves to a metric-alert grouptype crashes in Detector.detector_handler when `group_type.detector_handler(detector)` is instantiated. This conversion is not required by the PR's stated intent (adding the occurrence hook) — the stub could have stayed a plain DetectorHandler — and it is incomplete work: the TODO said 'This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction', but the abstraction is now adopted without any of the required methods implemented.

[ADVISORY] process_detectors' public return contract changes from list[tuple[Detector, list[DetectorEvaluationResult]]] to list[tuple[Detector, dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]]], but no consumer of the return value is updated anywhere in this diff. Any existing caller that iterates the per-detector results (e.g. `for result in detector_results:`) will now iterate group keys instead of DetectorEvaluationResult objects, silently producing wrong data or an AttributeError downstream; because dict iteration yields keys rather than raising, the breakage is silent rather than an obvious type error. This return-shape rework is work beyond the PR's stated scope of adding an occurrence hook and its blast radius is not addressed in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The new hook activates real occurrence production (the removed `# TODO: Add hook here for generating occurrence` means non-OK transitions now emit IssueOccurrence payloads) while Detector.project_id is still a hardcoded stub returning 1 (`# XXX: Temporary property until we add project_id to the model`). The occurrence construction pattern this hook mandates resolves project_id from the stub — the test's build_mock_occurrence_and_event demonstrates exactly this via `handler.detector.project_id` — so the first real StatefulDetectorHandler to fire will produce occurrences attributed to project 1, misrouting issue creation and any downstream workflow actions to the wrong project. The production path is switched on before its project dependency exists.

[ADVISORY] build_mock_occurrence_and_event never uses its `value` parameter and hardcodes identical occurrence id/event_id for every call, so the expected occurrences built in tests do not correspond to the packets under test. Tests construct expected occurrences with value=6 while the packets carry val1=8 (test_dedupe), val1=100 (test_results_on_change), and group_2=10 (test_state_results_multi_group), and every mock occurrence shares the same id/event_id — so a regression that passes the wrong value into build_occurrence_and_event_data or attaches an occurrence built for one group key to another group's result would still pass these assertions. The test suite cannot detect value propagation or cross-group mixup bugs in the hook path this PR introduces.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with a bare `pass`, leaving the three abstract methods (get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data) unimplemented, so the class remains abstract and raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class on any instantiation attempt. Previously a detector whose type resolves to this handler evaluated as a silent no-op (evaluate returned []). Now, `Detector.detector_handler` (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py) instantiates the handler class for any Detector row with this grouptype, and process_detectors crashes with TypeError instead of skipping — the sentinel behavior flipped from 'do nothing' to 'hard crash' for that type.

[ADVISORY] The newly activated occurrence-production path makes the placeholder `project_id` stub (`return 1` with 'XXX: Temporary property') load-bearing: the first concrete StatefulDetectorHandler will emit real IssueOccurrence payloads to Kafka attributed to project 1. This diff wires the TODO hook so StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now produces real occurrences via produce_occurrence_to_kafka (verified by test_state_results asserting the Kafka call). Every build_occurrence_and_event_data implementer reaches project_id through handler.detector.project_id, so before the stub is replaced, any live detector produces occurrences with evidence/occurrence rows bound to the wrong project (project 1), and the test suite codifies project_id=1 so the correction will require touching the assertion too.

[ADVISORY] The hook call `PriorityLevel(new_status)` silently casts DetectorPriorityLevel to PriorityLevel by raw integer value, coupling two distinct enums with no compile-time or runtime guard on value alignment. If DetectorPriorityLevel and PriorityLevel values drift (e.g., a new DetectorPriorityLevel tier is added or renumbered, while PriorityLevel is a different IntEnum with its own values), `PriorityLevel(new_status)` raises ValueError for a perfectly valid detector priority, crashing evaluation for that group key — and only the HIGH path is exercised by tests in this diff, so drift in any other tier is invisible until production. The typed-enum fix (a mapping or shared enum) is cheap now; after several handlers copy the cast, each site diverges independently.

[ADVISORY] Occurrence production to Kafka happens inside process_detectors before the handler's state updates are committed (commit_state_updates runs separately against the redis-backed state store), creating a non-atomic dual write. If the process crashes or the state commit fails after produce_occurrence_to_kafka succeeds, the redis state still shows the group key inactive, so the next packet for the same group key re-evaluates as a transition and produces a duplicate occurrence to the issues pipeline; the reverse ordering (commit then crash) silently drops the occurrence. No idempotency key ties the Kafka payload to the committed state transition, so both failure modes yield observable duplicates or loss on every crash mid-batch.

[ADVISORY] The abstract DetectorHandler.evaluate signature changed from returning list[DetectorEvaluationResult] to dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], and process_detectors now unconditionally calls detector_results.values() — any implementer not updated in this diff still returning a list crashes with AttributeError. process_detectors at line 60 does `for result in detector_results.values()`, which raises AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'values' for any DetectorHandler subclass outside this diff (in-repo handlers not touched here, or out-of-tree/plugin handlers) that still honors the old contract. The type system flags this only if the implementer's annotation is checked against the new ABC signature; duck-typed or loosely-annotated implementers compile and crash at runtime on the first evaluated packet for their grouptype.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with a `pass` body but does not implement the newly-abstract `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (nor `get_dedupe_value`/`get_group_key_values`), so instantiating it raises TypeError. The diff replaces a working no-op stub (old `evaluate` returned `[]`) with a class that cannot be instantiated: `StatefulDetectorHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data` is declared `@abc.abstractmethod` (processors/detector.py ~line 166), and `Detector.detector_handler` does `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so any detector registered with this group type crashes with `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract method build_occurrence_and_event_data` instead of returning a handler. The original 'TODO: Implement' stub was deliberately inert; this PR silently flips it to a broken inheritor without implementing the required hook.

[ADVISORY] The `DetectorHandler.evaluate` contract silently changed from `list[DetectorEvaluationResult]` to `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, and `process_detectors` now unconditionally calls `detector_results.values()`, so any handler subclass that still returns a list crashes with AttributeError at runtime rather than failing at the type boundary. Out-of-tree or not-yet-updated in-tree `DetectorHandler` subclasses implementing `evaluate` with the old list contract will fail with `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'values'` inside `process_detectors` for every data packet, killing detector evaluation for that handler. The abstract signature change (line ~126) is the only signal; nothing forces implementers to notice, and the removal of the duplicate-group-key guard means there is no defensive handling of the old shape either.

[ADVISORY] `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts a `value` parameter but never uses it, so the tests compare occurrences that are identical regardless of the value the handler actually passed. In `test_state_results_multi_group` the packet contains `group_2: 10` but the expected occurrence is built with `value=6`, and in `TestEvaluate.test_dedupe` the packet contains `val1: 8` while the expected occurrence uses `6` — all these assertions pass only because `value` is dropped on the floor. A regression that passes the wrong value (or drops it) into `build_occurrence_and_event_data` — the data that will feed evidence_data/priority in real handlers — would not be caught by any test in this diff; the hardcoded `6` also misleads future readers about the expected input.

[ADVISORY] The old code produced `result = None` for every non-OK transition (occurrence generation deferred behind a TODO); the new `else` branch produces an occurrence for *every* non-OK status change, including priority de-escalations on an already-active group (e.g. HIGH→MEDIUM), expanding behavior beyond the stated 'add hook' objective. For a group that is already active at HIGH and transitions to MEDIUM, the state change detection still fires (stored (active=True, HIGH) vs new (True, MEDIUM)), `enqueue_state_update` runs, and the new else branch now emits a full IssueOccurrence to Kafka with `initial_issue_priority=MEDIUM` — previously this path emitted nothing. If de-escalation occurrences were not part of the accepted intent, operators get duplicate/re-fired issues and workflow triggers on severity drops; nothing in the diff or test suite pins down that this transition class was consciously accepted (no test covers an active HIGH→MEDIUM transition).

[ADVISORY] `PriorityLevel(new_status)` hard-couples `DetectorPriorityLevel` and `PriorityLevel` by raw numeric value, raising ValueError the moment the two enums diverge. Today the tests only pass because `DetectorPriorityLevel.HIGH` and `PriorityLevel.HIGH` happen to share value 75 (the test at test_detector.py compares a `DetectorEvaluationResult` built with `PriorityLevel.HIGH` against one built with `DetectorPriorityLevel.HIGH` via this conversion). If either enum is later renumbered or gains a level independently — a plausible change since they live in different modules with different owners — every non-OK detector evaluation raises `ValueError` inside `evaluate_group_key_value`, taking down occurrence production for all stateful detectors. An explicit mapping or a shared level type would make the coupling a compile-time contract instead of a hidden runtime invariant.

[BUG] The newly wired occurrence-production path attributes every generated IssueOccurrence to Detector.project_id, which is hardcoded to return 1 ('# XXX: Temporary property until we add project_id to the model. return 1'), so occurrences built by build_occurrence_and_event_data (whose contract takes only group_key/value/new_status and has no project input) are created in project 1 regardless of which organization/project the detector belongs to. Once any real StatefulDetectorHandler implementation lands, create_issue_occurrence_to_kafka fires with project_id=1: metric-alert occurrences from every tenant are published into a single unrelated project, and the corresponding StatusChangeMessage resolution path (triggered on the OK transition) resolves groups in the wrong project — cross-tenant data placement and incorrect issue lifecycle mutation, not just a cosmetic misattribution.

[BUG] build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts a `value` parameter but never uses it in constructing the IssueOccurrence, so every test asserting the new occurrence-building hook passes a group value that disagrees with the packet it evaluates. TestEvaluate.test_results_on_change builds its expected occurrence with value=6 while the packet carries "val1": 100, TestEvaluate.test_dedupe builds with 6 while the packet carries 8, and test_state_results_multi_group builds occurrence_2 with 6 while the packet carries "group_2": 10 — all still pass. A regression in evaluate_group_key_value that forwards the wrong group value (or drops `value` entirely) into build_occurrence_and_event_data is invisible to the entire suite, giving false confidence that the value flows correctly into the produced occurrence.

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler is changed from a concrete stub (evaluate returned []) to a bare subclass of StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing any of its abstract methods (get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), so instantiating it now raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class. The previous stub was instantiable and callable; any code path that resolves a Detector whose type is this slug and constructs its handler now crashes with TypeError instead of returning no results. The diff modifies no test touching grouptype.py or this handler (the only changed test file, tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py, exercises only the local MockDetectorStateHandler), so this regression ships completely unverified — the old stub had TODO coverage expectations that are now silently gone.

[ADVISORY] TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds its expected occurrence via build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...) while the expected DetectorEvaluationResult it is compared against declares group_key="group_key", so the expected fixture describes two different groups at once. The pre-existing evaluate_group_key_value call in this test (unchanged outside the diff, and pinned to "group_key" by the old passing assertion) produces an occurrence fingerprinted from "group_key", not "val1". Either the equality assertion fails outright, or — if build_fingerprint does not incorporate the group key — the test passes while never exercising a fingerprint that distinguishes group keys, and the "val1" argument silently misleads every future reader of this fixture.

[ADVISORY] The only process_detectors tests for the stateful handler (test_state_results, test_state_results_multi_group) exercise the transition to HIGH and assert produce_occurrence_to_kafka with status_change=None; no test in the diff drives a stateful detector through a resolve (OK) transition via process_detectors, where result.result is now a non-None StatusChangeMessage. process_detectors now unconditionally calls create_issue_occurrence_from_result for any non-None result, and that path can now receive either an IssueOccurrence or a StatusChangeMessage depending on the transition direction. Checked file: tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py (the only test file changed in this diff) — it covers the occurrence branch end-to-end with mock assertions but never the status-change branch through process_detectors, so a regression mis-wiring status_change or feeding a StatusChangeMessage down the occurrence serialization path passes the suite. (TestEvaluate.test_above_below_threshold covers the OK branch only at the evaluate() level, bypassing process_detectors and the Kafka producer entirely.)

[BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler with `pass`, leaving the abstract methods get_group_key_values and build_occurrence_and_event_data unimplemented, so the class can no longer be instantiated or evaluated without raising TypeError, where the previous implementation safely returned [] and produced no results. Any Detector row whose type slug resolves to this handler now crashes the process_detectors loop with a TypeError (unimplemented abstract method) instead of evaluating to no results; a single misconfigured or future-created detector of this type turns the evaluation batch into an error instead of a no-op.

[ADVISORY] The duplicate-group-key guard in process_detectors (the 'Duplicate detector state group keys found' logger.error plus skip) was removed and replaced by `results[result.group_key] = result` in evaluate, which silently overwrites the earlier result with no log and no metric, and the regression test covering that path (test_state_results_multi_group_dupe) was deleted. If a subclass's evaluate_group_key_value (or an overridden evaluate) ever returns results whose group_key collides, the earlier DetectorEvaluationResult — including its already-built IssueOccurrence — is silently dropped with no error signal, and the removed 'we should investigate this' observability is gone; the anomaly the previous code explicitly guarded against is now invisible.

[ADVISORY] This diff enables occurrence production for stateful detectors (previously result was always None), so create_issue_occurrence_from_result now fires produce_occurrence_to_kafka inside process_detectors before commit_state_updates runs in the caller, and a Kafka delivery failure leaves the detector state and dedupe value committed with the alert never delivered and never retried. If the Kafka produce for a newly-triggering group fails (delivery is asynchronous and not surfaced to this path), the group is already marked active and its dedupe value advanced, so every subsequent evaluation of the same condition no-ops ('already active' / dedupe skip) — the alert is permanently lost while the system reports the packet as successfully processed. This failure path did not exist for stateful detectors before this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler with `pass`, leaving the abstract methods get_group_key_values and build_occurrence_and_event_data unimplemented, so the class can no longer be instantiated or evaluated without raising TypeError, where the previous implementation safely returned [] and produced no results. Any Detector row whose type slug resolves to this handler now crashes the process_detectors loop with a TypeError (unimplemented abstract method) instead of evaluating to no results; a single misconfigured or future-created detector of this type turns the evaluation batch into an error instead of a no-op.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py`, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed from a concrete `DetectorHandler` with an `evaluate()` implementation returning `[]` to `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass`. In `src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py`, `StatefulDetectorHandler` has abstract requirements (`get_group_key_values` and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, plus any other abstract methods it defines), so a subclass with `pass` remains abstract and cannot be instantiated. Since `Detector.detector_handler` instantiates the handler class (`group_type.detector_handler(self)`) and `process_detectors` does not catch `TypeError`, any detector using this handler would raise at runtime instead of being a no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The duplicate-group-key guard in process_detectors (the 'Duplicate detector state group keys found' logger.error plus skip) was removed and replaced by `results[result.group_key] = result` in evaluate, which silently overwrites the earlier result with no log and no metric, and the regression test covering that path (test_state_results_multi_group_dupe) was deleted. If a subclass's evaluate_group_key_value (or an overridden evaluate) ever returns results whose group_key collides, the earlier DetectorEvaluationResult — including its already-built IssueOccurrence — is silently dropped with no error signal, and the removed 'we should investigate this' observability is gone; the anomaly the previous code explicitly guarded against is now invisible.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the explicit duplicate-group-key detection/logging in `process_detectors` (the loop/`logger.error("Duplicate detector state group keys found")` block is deleted) and the associated test `test_state_results_multi_group_dupe` is also removed. The new `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` builds a dict via `results[result.group_key] = result`, which would overwrite on collisions with no log/metric. However, with the new API shape (`get_group_key_values` returns a `dict` and `evaluate` returns a `dict`), duplicates from input are no longer representable in the same way as the old list-based path, so this is not a clearly verifiable correctness regression from the diff alone—more a loss of defensive observability if a handler returns inconsistent/colliding keys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] This diff enables occurrence production for stateful detectors (previously result was always None), so create_issue_occurrence_from_result now fires produce_occurrence_to_kafka inside process_detectors before commit_state_updates runs in the caller, and a Kafka delivery failure leaves the detector state and dedupe value committed with the alert never delivered and never retried. If the Kafka produce for a newly-triggering group fails (delivery is asynchronous and not surfaced to this path), the group is already marked active and its dedupe value advanced, so every subsequent evaluation of the same condition no-ops ('already active' / dedupe skip) — the alert is permanently lost while the system reports the packet as successfully processed. This failure path did not exist for stateful detectors before this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does newly enable occurrence creation for stateful detectors: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` now builds an `IssueOccurrence` via `build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` for non-OK transitions, after calling `self.enqueue_state_update(...)`, and `process_detectors` now calls `create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)` for each returned result before any `commit_state_updates` is invoked in this function. This establishes an ordering where side effects (Kafka production inside `create_issue_occurrence_from_result`) happen separately from, and earlier than, persistence of the detector's dedupe/state updates (committed later by the caller). However, the claim that a Kafka delivery failure is asynchronous, not surfaced here, and would still allow state/dedupe to be committed (causing permanent alert loss) is not directly verifiable from this diff because the behavior/error handling of `create_issue_occurrence_from_result`/`produce_occurrence_to_kafka` and when/if the caller commits state are not shown. It is nonetheless a concrete, diff-grounded reliability/atomicity concern introduced by this change, but not a proven defect from the diff alone.
